Subject: Live inference capacity playbook — recap & immediate next steps

Hi Samantha / Alex —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our call and the set of short actions we agreed on so we can move toward a pilot. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Pain points you described
- Perceived streaming UX degradation: end users see chunking/stutters when responses stream (most noticeable on mobile).
- p95 latency spikes: observed p95s in the 600–800ms range during peak windows for the streaming endpoint.
- Concurrency limits: bursts during peak hours produce 429s and queuing — you mentioned reconfiguring autoscaler didn’t smooth it out.
- Memory/KV pressure with long context (several long conversations up to ~8k tokens) causing degraded throughput.
- Security requirement: must run within a VPC and provide audit logs for the pilot.

Current stack (as I understood it)
- Models served via in-house Triton-based service behind a gRPC gateway running on GKE.
- GPU pool is shared across teams, small NVIDIA A100 slices; no dedicated capacity today.
- Frontend does token-chunked streaming over WebSocket; client expects chunk latencies < 80ms for smooth UX.

Success criteria you listed
- p95 single-request latency <= 250ms for short prompts at sustained concurrency of 50–75.
- Streaming chunk arrival jitter < 80ms for top 90% of chunks.
- 99.9% of requests succeed (429s < 0.1%).
- Pilot must run inside your VPC and meet audit/logging requirements.

Proposed immediate next steps
1) You share a 30–60 minute sample prompt set + a short trace window (we can use the metrics you attached). I’ve included a stub attachment for what we usually ask for. (attachment: sample_prompts.json)
2) Redwood will run a short, non-invasive load test (no production writes) using a controlled harness and replicate the streaming pattern you described.
3) Marcus / Karthik will run a quick review of traces and follow up with a hypothesis on the bottleneck (kernel/CUDA scheduling, batching config, KV-cache eviction).
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive (60 minutes) to review test results and discuss Dedicated capacity pilot parameters — propose Wed Mar 24, 10:00–11:00 PT. Calendly link below.

Attachments: system_metrics-20270322.zip (metrics + small trace), sample_prompts.json
Shared link: https://drive.redwood.com/open?id=1A2b3C-system-traces-omnidrve

If this aligns, I’ll queue the load test for tomorrow and loop in our infra team for the VPC checklist.

Thanks,

Thanks Tessa — this is a solid summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Prompt / usage shape: average prompt length ~120 tokens; frequent follow-on context bumps the context window to ~6–8k tokens in heavy sessions.
- Streaming behavior: client streams in 250–300ms chunk intervals now, but end-users report visible pauses when a chunk takes >250ms. So your chunk jitter target matches our expectations.
- Traffic pattern: we have two 30–45 minute peaks UTC 16:00–17:00 and 01:00–01:45 with sudden surges tied to events. Peak instantaneous concurrency can hit ~120 connections to the streaming endpoint.
- Security: VPC peering + access to audit logs is required for the pilot. We can provide a jumpbox and allow the load test harness to use a whitelisted IP.

We’ll attach a 20-minute skyline trace and the sample prompt deck by EOD (sending separately). 

We can do Wed Mar 24 10:00 PT for the deep-dive — that works for Alex and me. Budget note: we have a constrained pilot budget but can consider a short Dedicated trial if we see measurable latency improvements.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Sam

Thanks Sam / Tessa — quick engineering follow-up and asks before we kick the harness off: 

1) Can you share a single request/response trace (raw timing) for a session that shows the chunking stutter? Preferably the client-side websocket timings and the server-side per-token timing. If you’re not able to share client logs, server traces with per-operator timing are OK.
2) Confirm the model size(s) and tokenizer you’re running (e.g., 7B, 13B; tokenizer: sentencepiece/bpe). If you have quantized artifacts mention the format.
3) Are you using any custom attention masking / long-context tweaks? That can materially impact kernel selection and memory usage.
4) For the bandwidth/throughput test, we’ll run two scenarios: (A) steady concurrency to 75 qps for 15 minutes, (B) burst test to 120 concurrent streams with Poisson arrivals for 10 minutes. Please approve these for the staging cluster (no production writes).

What I’ll check first after we have traces: batching configuration, kernel-level stalls (small-batch kernel inefficiency), KV-cache eviction patterns, and gRPC gateway buffering. If there’s an obvious culprit we’ll share a short config patch (non-invasive) that you can apply in staging.

If you want, we can also run a quick one-off on Redwood Dedicated to show delta vs shared GPUs; that will need a short security checklist but is typically the fastest way to demonstrate predictable p95 behavior.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
